messages:
Lena (AE): Helix POC update — customer ran a synthetic burst warmup (60 parallel clients) and now reports intermittent 429s and TTFT spikes to 2-3s. Can SE/SRE triage? :thinking_face:
Jonah (SE): Yep. Do we know model/runtime and client config? Any client logs showing prefetch calls or batch sizing?
Lena (AE): They're on helios-13b-fp16. Typical prompts ~300 tokens, peaks ~800. Client used batch=24, prefetch=true and executed a all-clients prefetch script.
Tomas (ML): That pattern is a red flag. Simultaneous prefetches across many connections can blow out shard working sets and cause KV churn. Large batch sizes plus long contexts slow batch formation too.
Priya (SRE): Infra view: saw tenant egress at ~95% around 2056001050, router ingress backlog and our per-tenant concurrency guard opened and returned 429s. Also observed frequent KV shard evictions at 2056001065 which reduces prefix hit-rate and increases TTFT.
Jonah (SE): Why evictions from prefetch?
Tomas (ML): Each client prefetched different prefixes, expanding per-shard memory use so LRU kicks in. Combine with memory used by decoding buffers for batch=24 and you get cache thrash. Result: less cache hit, more work per request, higher TTFT.
Lena (AE): Customer insists they need the parallelism to simulate peak load. Will Dedicated fix this?
Priya (SRE): Dedicated helps isolate egress and cache from noisy neighbors, but doesn't remove bad warmup patterns. Immediate mitigations: 1) stop simultaneous global prefetch; 2) set batch.max_requests=8-12; 3) enable streaming so first bytes return sooner; 4) stage prefetch per-shard or stagger clients with jittered delays.
Jonah (SE): Example client snippet to send them:
```json
{"batch": {"max_requests": 12, "max_delay_ms": 8}, "prefetch": "staged", "stream": true}
```
Lena (AE): Explain "staged"?
Tomas (ML): Use /v1/prefetch?mode=staged which sequences prefetch per shard server-side, or have clients add random jitter before prefetch calls to avoid lockstep.
Priya (SRE): I can temporarily raise their concurrency cap from 30 -> 48 for 90 minutes while they replay a controlled ramp and watch queue depth and eviction metrics. Will rollback if risk increases. :white_check_mark:
QuokkaBot: alert/tenant/helix-poc: concurrency cap increased at 2056001115 by Priya (SRE). Monitoring enabled.
Jonah (SE): Also ask customer to capture 3 traces with X-Trace-Id: one during warmup, one steady-state, one during a spike. That will show time split across gateway/router/runtime and confirm where waiting happens.
Lena (AE): They also asked for a rough Dedicated monthly number to justify the trial. Anything we can share now?
Priya (SRE): Rough thumb: an 8xGPU Dedicated pod baseline ~ "$Yk/month" plus networking/egress premium. For POC we sometimes offer a short trial of a pre-warmed Dedicated node with temporary uplift; Sales Ops must formalize pricing.
Jonah (SE): For presales framing: "Hosted + tuned warmup (staggered prefetch, smaller batch, streaming) is usually the cheapest for POC. Dedicated is best when you need predictable latency under sustained high concurrency and to isolate egress/cache pressure"
Tomas (ML): Note: switching quantization (FP4) or alternative kernels may change per-token cost at long contexts — we should re-bench if they change quant/profile.
Lena (AE): Action items: 1) ask customer to run staged/staggered prefetch with jitter, set batch.max_requests=12, enable stream=true; 2) collect 3 traces and attach X-Trace-Id; 3) Priya to apply temporary concurrency bump and monitor evictions/queues; 4) I'll loop in Sales Ops for Dedicated trial quoting.
Priya (SRE): I'll watch eviction rate and queue depth. If eviction rate drops and TTFT improves we keep the bump for the window.
Lena (AE): Thanks all. I'll send the sample config to the customer and request traces. Re-open thread if they still see 429s or TTFT > 1s. :raised_hands:
